claims.text: Corrosion protection in uncoated, pre-exposed Q235 steel is governed by the formation and stability of its native iron oxide film.
At room temperature, Q235 steel forms a thin, adherent, relatively compact native oxide layer.
The room-temperature native oxide layer retards further corrosion of Q235 steel.
At 700–900 °C in aggressive salt environments, thermal activation accelerates oxidation kinetics in Q235 steel.
At 700–900 °C, thermal stresses cause the native oxide on Q235 steel to develop into a thicker, porous, non-adherent scale.
The high-temperature oxide scale is prone to spallation and chloride penetration.
Spallation and chloride penetration increase corrosion degradation of the underlying Q235 steel.
As-received Q235 steel has a native oxide film formed in ambient atmosphere.
The morphology, continuity, adherence, porosity, and thickness of the native oxide vary with exposure temperature and mediate protection.
Slow room-temperature oxidation produces a coherent physical barrier to corrosive agents.
Enhanced oxidation and thermal-expansion mismatch at elevated temperature cause oxide growth and loss of cohesion.
A porous oxide permits chloride ions to reach and attack the underlying steel.
High-temperature salt exposure will cause greater mass change than room-temperature salt exposure.
High-temperature exposure will produce a thicker, more porous, and less adherent oxide layer than room-temperature exposure.
Q235 steel will have a higher measured corrosion rate at high temperature than at room temperature.
At room temperature, the native oxide on uncoated Q235 steel remains relatively protective and the corrosion rate is low.
A (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 HEA coating on Q235 steel has good corrosion resistance in NaCl solution because of a dense passivation film.
Engineered HEA coatings containing elements such as Cr and Nb can alter the passivation mechanism relative to uncoated Q235 steel.
The proposed native-oxide mechanism should not be applied to substantially different salt compositions or exposure durations.
